dict.string: ChirpChirps uses Bluetooth to find nearby people running ChirpChirps and connect to them directly for push-to-talk and messages.
ChirpChirps uses the camera when you tap the camera button in a chat, so you can take a photo and send it to people nearby.
ChirpChirps uses your local network to connect directly to nearby phones over Wi-Fi for push-to-talk and messages, without the internet.
ChirpChirps shares your position on the map only for a check-in you start by hand. Each check-in lasts 15 minutes, is sent directly to nearby devices, and never resumes on its own.
ChirpChirps uses the microphone so you can talk to nearby people with push-to-talk and record voice messages for them.
ChirpChirps saves a photo someone nearby sent you to your library when you tap Save on it.
ChirpChirps uses on-device speech recognition to show live captions of what nearby people say over push-to-talk.
